records.title: Introduction
records.objectiveSourceExtract: s Upon completion of the lesson, participants will be able to: ▪ Identify UNPOL CBD activities, ▪ Understand the long-term impact of CBD vs. short-term impact of UNPOL operations, ▪ Recognize the connection between CBD and the intended end-state/exit strategy of UNPOL and to ▪ State different phases of the CBD process.
records.objectives: Identify CBD activities; distinguish long-term CBD from short-term operations; relate CBD to end-state/exit strategy; state process phases
records.requiredContent: Purpose/impact, ownership, sustainability and six-phase process
records.methodsAndActivity: Interactive orientation and review; no standalone numbered CARANA exercise
records.trace: Objectives p. 2; duration p. 4; content pp. 5–15
records.facilitatorBoundary: Facilitator prompts; no numbered model-outcome key located

records.title: Situational Analysis
records.objectiveSourceExtract: s Learners will be able to:  Specify analytical skills  Deconstruct policing practice  Understand the SSR process, relevant structures, and impact of politics  Compare local with international policing practices  Demonstrate cultural and inter-personal sensitivity and the impacts of change on individuals and organisations as well as to:  Appreciate analysis as a methodology  Understand the situation they encounter in specific mission, organizational, unit, departmental settings  Understand the role of various actors and their relevance/impact on CBD  Analyse police processes and practices and identify reform opportunities  Appreciate the importance and purpose of setting a baseline Throughout this lesson, make sure to not only introduce the tools for analysis but also explain to participants how the tools interlink. Additionally, point out why the exact sequencing of the steps outlined throughout this lesson is very important.
records.duration: 7 hours 35 minutes: presentation 60 minutes; exercise 6 hours 35 minutes
records.objectives: Specify analysis; deconstruct policing practice; understand SSR/politics; compare policing practices; demonstrate sensitivity; analyse actors, processes, reform opportunities and baseline
records.requiredContent: Conflict/response/CBD analysis; PESTEL-S, PIN, conflict tools; stakeholders; 5×6 areas/dimensions; SWOT; baseline
records.methodsAndActivity: 1.1 small-group analysis, matrix/SWOT, presentation/reflection; participant annexes A–C/E
records.trace: Objectives p. 2; duration p. 4; content pp. 5–19; activity pp. 20–33; handouts pp. 37–48
records.facilitatorBoundary: Expected outcomes pp. 23–33 and Annex D p. 47; pp. 20–21 say defer Annex D until after the activity

records.requiredContent: Strategic alignment, SDG16, prioritisation, sustainability, SMART, performance framework
records.methodsAndActivity: 2.1 groups identify 6–10 objectives from L1 analysis, score/prioritise ignoring risk category, phrase top two as SMART; present and reflect
